hero.title: Healthcare, wherever life takes you

hero.note: Designed with privacy in mind. No account required.

problem.title: Getting healthcare abroad shouldn't feel overwhelming.
problem.subtitle: When you don't speak the local language, even simple healthcare interactions can become stressful. Explaining how you feel, understanding medical instructions, or knowing where to go shouldn't make getting care harder.

words.quote: I don't know how to explain what I'm feeling.
words.title: Finding the right words
words.body: Describing symptoms in another language can be difficult, especially when you're already feeling unwell and anxious. Nuance often gets lost in auto-translation apps.

info.title: Understanding medical information
info.body: Prescriptions, consultation notes, and discharge instructions can be hard to understand in an unfamiliar script, leaving patients uncertain about dosaging and aftercare.

where.quote: Should I visit a pharmacy or a doctor?
where.title: Knowing where to go
where.body: Every country has its own healthcare system, referral expectations, and triage levels. Knowing where to start is not always straightforward for an outsider.

how.title:
Making healthcare easier to understand,
wherever you are.
how.subtitle:
WellAbroad helps you explain your symptoms in another language,
understand medical documents, and feel more prepared when navigating healthcare abroad.

questions.title: The right questions help you find the right words.
questions.body: Guided questions help users describe their symptoms, organise relevant information, and prepare a structured bilingual summary to show a doctor or pharmacist. Users can review their answers before generating or sharing the summary.

documents.title: Make sense of your medical information.
documents.body: Upload or scan a prescription, medical report, or consultation note to get a translation and a plain-language explanation of active ingredients, dosages, and precautions. WellAbroad helps you understand your documents with clarity, without diagnosing or replacing healthcare advice.

summary.title: Take your summary with you.
summary.body: Export or print a clear, bilingual clinical intake sheet ready for reception or the attending doctor, ensuring your medical history and current concerns are communicated accurately.

useCases.title:
Different situations.
One less language barrier.
useCases.subtitle: Whether you are traveling for a week, recovering from a doctor's visit, or relocating long-term, WellAbroad adapts to your medical context.

travelling.title: When you're travelling
travelling.body: You feel unwell abroad and need to explain your symptoms at a local pharmacy or clinic quickly and clearly without misinterpretations.

consultation.title: After a consultation
consultation.body: You receive a document in a language you don't fully understand and need help making sense of dosages, active ingredients, and care steps.

settling.title: Settling into a new country
settling.body: You need to understand how to navigate the local healthcare system, find reliable primary care, and register your health history accurately.

privacy.title: Health data that never leaves your hands.
privacy.body: We believe medical privacy shouldn't require technical expertise or blind trust. WellAbroad is built without accounts, without cloud retention, and without diagnostic pretensions. Your symptoms and prescriptions are deciphered locally in your browser, helping you communicate clearly in a foreign clinic; and vanishing completely the moment your conversation ends.
privacy.tagline: Designed for travelers and expats · Zero persistent data · Ephemeral by default

finalCta.title:

when you need care abroad.
finalCta.subtitle: WellAbroad helps you explain your symptoms, understand medical documents, and navigate local healthcare in a language you understand.

symptoms.disclaimerWith: WellAbroad is a medical communication aid, not a diagnostic service. In an emergency, call {number}.

PK.name: Pakistan
PK.note: Pakistan has no single nationwide emergency number, and 1122 is run provincially, so coverage varies by area. 112 may not work reliably. Operators may speak limited English.

US.name: United States
US.note: Emergency rooms must see anyone in an emergency, and bills can be high. Ask about costs for non-emergency care.

GB.name: United Kingdom
GB.note: 999 is for emergencies. For urgent problems that are not life-threatening, use NHS 111 or an urgent treatment centre.

DE.name: Germany
DE.note: 112 is for life-threatening situations. Call 116 117 for urgent medical needs outside practice hours.

FR.name: France
FR.note: 112 works everywhere in France. 15 reaches the SAMU directly for medical emergencies.
